subject: natural-sciences-tech
description: Natural Sciences & Technology skill tree. Intermediate Phase (Gr 4–6), CAPS. One strand per term: T1 Life and Living, T2 Matter and Materials, T3 Energy and Change, T4 Planet Earth and Beyond. Technology (Structures / Processing / Systems & Control) is woven into each strand. Topics do not prerequisite each other — all unlocked from day one.

levels.title: Grade 4 — Natural Sciences & Technology
levels.description: CAPS Intermediate Phase Grade 4. 18 topics across the year, 3½ hours/week. Topics do not prerequisite each other — all unlocked from day one.

atomic_skills.title: Living and non-living things
atomic_skills.description: Differences between living plants and animals (seven life processes — feeding, growing, reproducing, breathing, excreting, sensing, moving) and non-living things. Germinating seeds, growing yeast.

atomic_skills.title: Structure of plants and animals
atomic_skills.description: Basic parts of plants (roots, stems, leaves, flowers, fruits, seeds) and animals (head, tail, body, limbs, sense organs). Visible differences between species.

atomic_skills.title: What plants need to grow
atomic_skills.description: Plants need light, water and air. New plants from cuttings and seeds. Seeds germinate with warmth and water.

atomic_skills.title: Habitats of animals
atomic_skills.description: Different habitats (grassland, forest, river, sea). Why animals need habitats for food, water, shelter, breeding and safety from danger.

atomic_skills.title: Structures for animal shelters
atomic_skills.description: Natural and human-made shelters. Shell vs frame structures. Designing an animal shelter for purpose, shape, size and materials.

atomic_skills.title: Materials around us
atomic_skills.description: Solids, liquids and gases and their properties. Changes of state through heating and cooling (melting, freezing, evaporating, condensing). The water cycle.

atomic_skills.title: Solid materials
atomic_skills.description: Raw materials (sand, clay, coal, oil, wood, plant fibre, animal wool/hide) and what they become. Properties: hard/soft, stiff/flexible, strong/weak, waterproof/absorbent.

atomic_skills.title: Strengthening materials
atomic_skills.description: Folding paper into circular, triangular or square pillars; rolling paper into struts. Investigating which shape supports the most weight.

atomic_skills.title: Strong frame structures
atomic_skills.description: Triangular struts in roof trusses, bridges, cranes, pylons, skeletons. Indigenous frame structures (Zulu uguqa, Xhosa rontabile/ungqu-phantsi, Nama matjieshuis).

atomic_skills.title: Energy and energy transfer
atomic_skills.description: Where energy for life comes from. Energy chain from the Sun → plants → animals/people.

atomic_skills.title: Energy around us
atomic_skills.description: Movement, heat, light, sound around us. Stored energy in food, wood, coal, oil products, natural gas. Input and output energy of common machines and appliances.

atomic_skills.title: Movement and energy in a system
atomic_skills.description: Musical instruments as systems with movement input (blowing, beating, plucking) and sound output. Indigenous musical instruments.

atomic_skills.title: Energy and sound
atomic_skills.description: Vibrations and sound. Loud/soft (volume), high/low (pitch). Noise pollution and protecting hearing.

atomic_skills.title: Planet Earth
atomic_skills.description: Earth as a sphere; land (rocks and soil), water, air; continents, oceans, islands. Earth as a planet in space.

atomic_skills.title: The Sun
atomic_skills.description: The Sun as our closest star — a ball of hot gas that gives heat and light. Very large, very far away.

atomic_skills.title: The Earth and the Sun
atomic_skills.description: Earth orbits the Sun. The Sun at the centre of the solar system. Earth as one of eight planets. The Sun's heat and light supports life.

atomic_skills.title: The Moon
atomic_skills.description: Moon as a ball of rock with no air or water. Phases of the Moon repeat every 29½ days. Cultural stories about the Moon.

atomic_skills.title: Rocket systems
atomic_skills.description: Rockets as systems to travel into space. Movement by pushing exhaust gases out the back. Designing and testing a balloon rocket.

levels.title: Grade 5 — Natural Sciences & Technology
levels.description: CAPS Intermediate Phase Grade 5. 17 topics across the year, 3½ hours/week. Topics do not prerequisite each other — all unlocked from day one.

atomic_skills.title: Plants and animals on Earth
atomic_skills.description: Biodiversity in South Africa. Inter-dependence of plants, animals and the resources in their habitats. Vertebrates and invertebrates.

atomic_skills.title: Animal skeletons
atomic_skills.description: Vertebrate skeletons: skull, backbone, ribs, limbs, shoulder/hip girdles. Skeletons protect organs and support movement (muscles and joints).

atomic_skills.title: Skeletons as structures
atomic_skills.description: Vertebrate skeleton as a frame structure. Some invertebrate skeletons as shell structures (e.g. crab). Modelling a skeleton from struts.

atomic_skills.title: Food chains
atomic_skills.description: Green plants make their own food and release oxygen. Herbivores, carnivores, omnivores. Energy flow from plant through animals in a food chain.

atomic_skills.title: Life cycles
atomic_skills.description: Stages in the life cycle of a plant (seed, seedling, adult, flowering, fruiting) and of a vertebrate animal. Generations, reproduction, care of young.

atomic_skills.title: Metals and non-metals
atomic_skills.description: Properties of metals (shiny, hard, strong, malleable, ductile, high melting point) vs solid non-metals (dull, brittle). Metals mined from the Earth.

atomic_skills.title: Uses of metals
atomic_skills.description: Metals conduct heat; some are magnetic; only iron rusts. Everyday uses: coins, wire, jewellery, furniture, buildings, bridges, vehicles, utensils, roofs.

atomic_skills.title: Processing materials
atomic_skills.description: Combining materials to make new ones — plaster of Paris, concrete, glue paste, dough, jelly, clay bricks. Properties change after processing.

atomic_skills.title: Processed materials
atomic_skills.description: Plaster, concrete, fabrics, ceramics, glass, plastics, paints and their special properties. Traditional African processing of clay pots, plant-fibre baskets and roofs.

atomic_skills.title: Stored energy in fuels
atomic_skills.description: Wood, coal, petrol, paraffin, gas, candle wax as fuels. Burning needs heat and oxygen. Fire safety in communities — causes, prevention, what to do.

atomic_skills.title: Energy and electricity
atomic_skills.description: Energy stored in cells/batteries. A circuit as a system to transfer electrical energy. From power station to home via pylons, substations and wiring. Electrical safety.

atomic_skills.title: Energy and movement
atomic_skills.description: Stretched/twisted elastic and compressed springs store energy. Releasing gives movement energy — catapults, elastic-powered aeroplanes, jack-in-the-box.

atomic_skills.title: Systems for moving things
atomic_skills.description: Vehicles use wheels and axles to move easily. Identifying and making wheels-and-axles in everyday vehicles.

atomic_skills.title: Planet Earth
atomic_skills.description: Earth orbits the Sun (a year ≈ 365 days). Earth spins on its axis (a day ≈ 24 hours).

atomic_skills.title: Surface of the Earth
atomic_skills.description: Earth's crust — rocks and soil. Topsoil formed from broken-down rocks. Sandy, clayey, loamy soils and what they hold. Importance of conserving topsoil.

atomic_skills.title: Sedimentary rocks
atomic_skills.description: How sedimentary rocks form over time from layers of mud and sand. Shale, sandstone, limestone and their uses (cement, building stone).

atomic_skills.title: Fossils
atomic_skills.description: Body and trace fossils preserved in sedimentary rock. South Africa's fossil record — the Coelacanth, African dinosaurs, and the Cradle of Humankind.

levels.title: Grade 6 — Natural Sciences & Technology
levels.description: CAPS Intermediate Phase Grade 6. 20 topics across the year, 3½ hours/week. Topics do not prerequisite each other — all unlocked from day one.

atomic_skills.title: Photosynthesis
atomic_skills.description: Plants make glucose from sunlight, carbon dioxide and water. Plants store some as starch and release oxygen. Testing foods for starch with iodine.

atomic_skills.title: Nutrients in food
atomic_skills.description: Four nutrient groups: carbohydrates, proteins, fats and oils, vitamins and minerals. Natural vs processed foods. Reading food labels for additives.

atomic_skills.title: Nutrition
atomic_skills.description: A balanced diet draws from all four nutrient groups plus water and fibre. Diet-related conditions — tooth decay, obesity, diabetes, deficiency diseases.

atomic_skills.title: Food processing
atomic_skills.description: Processing makes food edible (cooking), longer-lasting (preserving) or more nutritious (fermenting). Methods: combining, cooking, freezing, pickling, drying, salting.

atomic_skills.title: Ecosystems and food webs
atomic_skills.description: Different ecosystems (rivers, mountains, sea, ponds, wetlands, grasslands, forests, deserts). Producers, consumers (herbivores/carnivores/omnivores) and decomposers in a food web.

atomic_skills.title: Solids, liquids and gases
atomic_skills.description: All matter is made of particles. Particle arrangement differs in each state — close-packed regular (solid), close-packed irregular (liquid), far apart (gas).

atomic_skills.title: Mixtures
atomic_skills.description: Mixtures of solids, of solids and liquids, of two liquids. Separating by sieving, filtering, hand sorting, settling and decanting.

atomic_skills.title: Solutions as special mixtures
atomic_skills.description: Soluble vs insoluble substances. Saturated solutions. Recovering the solute by evaporating the solvent (crystallisation).

atomic_skills.title: Dissolving
atomic_skills.description: Factors that change how fast a solute dissolves — temperature, stirring/shaking, grain size. Fair-test investigations.

atomic_skills.title: Mixtures and water resources
atomic_skills.description: Water pollution from soluble and insoluble substances and water-borne illnesses. Importance of natural wetlands for habitats and water quality.

atomic_skills.title: Processes to purify water
atomic_skills.description: Sieving, filtering, settling, decanting, boiling and adding chemicals to clean water. Designing and making a simple sand filter.

atomic_skills.title: Electric circuits
atomic_skills.description: A simple circuit: cell/battery, conducting wires, output device (bulb/buzzer/motor), switch. Drawing circuit diagrams with standard symbols.

atomic_skills.title: Electrical conductors and insulators
atomic_skills.description: Most metals conduct electricity; most non-metals (plastic, rubber, glass, ceramic) do not. Where insulators are used in real life.

atomic_skills.title: Systems to solve problems
atomic_skills.description: Circuits solve real problems — street lighting, alarms, traffic lights, fans, heaters. Designing a system with cells, wires, bulbs/buzzers and switches.

atomic_skills.title: Mains electricity
atomic_skills.description: Coal as a fossil fuel and its use in power stations. Cost of electricity. Danger of illegal connections. Renewable ways to generate electricity (wind, solar, hydro).

atomic_skills.title: The Solar System
atomic_skills.description: Sun at the centre, eight planets (Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune) and the asteroid belt. Rocky vs gas planets. Moons.

atomic_skills.title: Movements of the Earth and planets
atomic_skills.description: Rotation: Earth spins on its axis once every 24 hours (day and night). Revolution: Earth travels around the Sun once every 365¼ days (a year).

atomic_skills.title: The movement of the Moon
atomic_skills.description: The Moon spins on its axis and revolves around the Earth — both take about 28 days. Together, Earth and Moon revolve around the Sun.

atomic_skills.title: Systems for looking into space
atomic_skills.description: Telescopes gather information from space. South Africa hosts some of the world's largest — SALT (Southern African Large Telescope) and SKA (Square Kilometre Array).

atomic_skills.title: Systems to explore the Moon and Mars
atomic_skills.description: Moon Rovers carried astronauts; Mars Rovers explore Mars remotely. Their wheels and axles, cameras, mechanical arms and solar power. Building a model vehicle.
